cases.subject: C++
cases.question: What is a default constructor in C++?
expected_facts: A default constructor can be called without arguments; default arguments can satisfy this.
cases.answer:
A default constructor is a type of constructor that requires no parameters when called, and it is a member function named after the type it constructs. [C++ Notes for Professionals, PDF p. 240]

The compiler implicitly provides an empty default constructor when certain conditions are met, such as when no other types of constructors are defined. [C++ Notes for Professionals, PDF p. 240]

cases.question: What is the difference between malloc and calloc in C?

cases.answer:
calloc initializes all bits of the allocated memory to zero, whereas malloc does not. [C Notes for Professionals, PDF p. 268]

calloc takes the number of elements and the size of each element as arguments, whereas malloc takes the total size in bytes. [C Notes for Professionals, PDF p. 268] [C Notes for Professionals, PDF p. 267]

cases.question: Must equal Java objects have equal hashCode values, and can unequal objects share a hash code?
expected_facts: Equal objects require equal hash codes; unequal objects may collide.
cases.answer:
If two objects are equal according to the equals method, calling hashCode on each of them must produce the same integer result. [javaNotesForProfessionals, PDF p. 253] [javaNotesForProfessionals, PDF p. 257]

It is not required that unequal objects produce distinct hash code integer results, meaning unequal objects can share a hash code. [javaNotesForProfessionals, PDF p. 253]

cases.subject: Python
cases.question: Why can a mutable default argument retain values between function calls?
expected_facts: Default argument objects are created at definition time and can be reused/mutated across calls.
cases.answer:
A mutable default argument retains values between function calls because default arguments are initialized once at the point when the function is defined, rather than when the function is called. [Python Notes for Professionals, PDF p. 215]

The default values are stored inside the function object's __defaults__ member variable, meaning successive calls are not guaranteed to have the initial default value if the argument is mutated. [Python Notes for Professionals, PDF p. 215]

cases.question: How do constructors and destructors work in C++?
expected_facts: Explain creation/initialization by constructors and destruction/cleanup by destructors.
cases.answer:
A constructor initializes objects, with default constructors requiring no parameters and initializing member variables or executing complex logic in their body. [C++ Notes for Professionals, PDF p. 240]

A destructor is a function without arguments prefixed with a tilde that is automatically called when an object is about to be destroyed to clean up resources, such as releasing dynamically allocated memory. [C++ Notes for Professionals, PDF p. 242]

Lists are enclosed in brackets, whereas tuples are enclosed in parentheses. [Python Notes for Professionals, PDF p. 59]

The elements and size of a list can be changed, while tuples are immutable and fixed-length, meaning items cannot be added, modified, or removed once initialized. [Python Notes for Professionals, PDF p. 59] [Python Notes for Professionals, PDF p. 186] [Python Notes for Professionals, PDF p. 42]

Lists have methods like append and extend, which tuples do not have. [Python Notes for Professionals, PDF p. 186]
